name: Think-Pair-Share
ordered_paraphrased_procedure: Present a question and allow independent thinking and responses.
Pair learners nearby.
A shares with B, then B with A. Clarify reasons for disagreement; a joint response is optional.
key_peer_dependency: Both responses must become available for comparison.
artifact_flow: Private ideas → exchanged explanations → optional joint response/class contribution.
nonnegotiable_mechanism: Protected individual thought precedes reciprocal pair exchange.
important_variants: Written preparation and class reporting are instructor choices; online adaptation uses paired communication.
evidence_limit: All numbered core steps rechecked in the licensed second-edition book on2026-10-15. Task-specific parameters and optional variants remain distinct. Narrative paragraphs can truncate in accessibility; no claim of reading every case example word for word. This is procedural grounding, not method-specific efficacy or prevalence evidence.

name: Role-Play
ordered_paraphrased_procedure: Form groups large enough for the stakeholder roles.
Present and clarify the scenario; allow questions.
Assign stakeholder and any moderator/observer roles and clarify duties.
Set a time limit or other stopping condition.
Enact until the target behavior, characteristic or skill becomes clear.
Debrief role interpretations, motivations and consequences in groups or as a class.
Optionally reenact with different characters or a revised scenario and debrief again.
participants_grouping: Groups large enough for the scenario’s stakeholder roles.
key_peer_dependency: Action depends on responding from different stakeholder positions.
artifact_flow: Scenario → enacted decisions/dialogue → interpretation/debrief; optional reenactment.
nonnegotiable_mechanism: Assumed perspectives must be enacted and interpreted.
important_variants: Role swap; observed performance; Triad Listening: speaker/listener/referee.

name: Analytic Teams
ordered_paraphrased_procedure: Form groups of four or five and allocate specific analytic roles and duties.
Present a common lecture, video or reading.
Allow individuals to share findings and jointly prepare an oral or written analysis.
Close in a way that highlights role contributions, using a brief report, panel or poster format appropriate to the task.
participants_grouping: Groups of4–5 in the book; distinct analytic functions on one source.
roles: Proponent; critic; example giver; summarizer; questioner, as appropriate.
key_peer_dependency: A fuller analysis requires distinct functions applied to the same material.
artifact_flow: Common source → individual role analysis → team exchange → reports.
nonnegotiable_mechanism: Divide analytic responsibilities rather than merely dividing source pages.
important_variants: Assign roles to whole teams; use different related assignments; extend across sessions.

name: Peer Editing
ordered_paraphrased_procedure: In pairs discuss the papers each plans to write; the partner takes notes, questions and suggests.
Research individually while also noticing resources useful to the partner.
Write individual drafts.
Exchange drafts, annotate them and complete a signed criteria-based review form.
Each author revises in light of the review.
Submit the final draft with its review form for instructor evaluation.
key_peer_dependency: A partner’s critical reading informs author revision.
artifact_flow: Idea talk → independent paper → reviewed draft → revision → submission.
nonnegotiable_mechanism: Reciprocal critique leads to author revision.
important_variants: Content/argument review as well as language editing.
